explanation: Transform a rate r into edge weight −log(r). A profitable product around a cycle becomes a negative cycle. Bellman–Ford starts all distances at zero so every component is covered; improvement on the nth pass detects a negative cycle. A small tolerance avoids roundoff-only improvements.
timeComplexity: O(n³): at most n passes each relax n² exchange edges, with constant work per edge.
spaceComplexity: O(n) distances; transformed edge weights are computed as needed rather than stored in another matrix.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: A cycle’s transformed weight is the negative logarithm of its exchange-rate product. It is negative exactly when that product exceeds one. Bellman–Ford relaxations from zero-valued distances cover every vertex; continuing improvement on the nth pass identifies a negative cycle, subject to the stated floating-point tolerance.
walkthrough: Rates 0→1=2 and 1→0=0.6 produce a round-trip multiplier of 1.2. Its negative-log weight is below zero, so the algorithm detects improvement around the cycle and returns true.
edgeCases: A rate product of exactly one is not profitable.
All components are covered by zero-initialized distances.
The small relaxation tolerance suppresses roundoff-only changes.
An empty rate matrix returns false.
